sources.title: Chandrayaan-3: Key Findings & Achievements in Lunar Exploration
sources.snippet:
* India’s Chandrayaan-3 mission, which successfully landed near the Moon’s south pole almost a year ago, has begun yielding significant scientific findings.
* The **Alpha Particle X-ray Spectrometer (APXS)** on the rover has provided new insights into the Moon’s surface composition and geological history.

# Findings from Chandrayaan 3 mission
## Description
* These findings, published in the journal **_Nature_** , support the hypothesis of a **lunar magma ocean (LMO) in the Moon’s early history** and suggest a churning of the lunar crust, potentially caused by an ancient asteroid impact.

sources.snippet:
Section: Chandrayaan-3 > Scientific results
* **Sulfur confirmed:** Pragyan's LIBS instrument made the first in-situ measurements near the south pole, unambiguously confirming sulfur, along with aluminium, calcium, iron, chromium and titanium.
* **First south-polar temperature profile:** ChaSTE measured ~50–80 °C at the surface plunging to about −170 °C just 10 cm below — a far steeper gradient than models predicted.

LIBS aboard Chandrayaan-3 confirmed Sulphur (S) on the lunar surface through unambiguous in-situ measurements [2].

The APXS experiment reported the first in situ measurements of elemental abundances in the lunar southern high-latitude regions [3]. Scientists estimated that Chandrayaan-3 ejected and displaced about 2.06 tonnes of lunar epiregolith over 108.4 mÂ² around the landing site [1].
